name: Vitamin/mineral supplements
anchor: No sovereign government sets a heavy-metal maximum for a pet supplement in a human-food basis. The instruments that reach the exact cell are pet-feed and animal-feed instruments. Japan's Pet Food Safety Act is the strongest of them: the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food are statutory, pet-scoped and recorded on an as-sold basis, and they set lead at 3000, cadmium at 1000 and inorganic arsenic at 2000 ug/kg (jp_petfood_2021_pb_3000, jp_petfood_2021_cd_1000, jp_petfood_2021_ias_2000) and set nothing for the remaining panel analytes. The EU feed instruments follow (Directive 2002/32/EC complementary feed for pet animals, mineral feed and trace-element feed additives under Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003), then FDA CVM compliance policy — which is named for completeness because it is routinely cited as the US pet-food metals floor, but which the register carries no row for, so it is disclosed here as a described floor rather than a cited one and is recorded as a register gap — then China's pet-feed guidance, which is draft and gated out of the register in any event. NASC's quality guidelines are voluntary and non-binding and are not a sovereign source at all. Every one of these floors is one hundred to three hundred times looser than the corresponding value published here, and every one is named on the cell it reaches. HMTc treats the feed instruments as a disclosed floor and anchors every published cell on the strictest applicable AS-SOLD child-protective human-food sovereign maximum, following Category 17's human-grade over-compliance and Category 16's child-protective supplement rule together. Where no as-sold sovereign value exists in any jurisdiction (aluminium, total chromium, hexavalent chromium, methylmercury) the cell is a control: mandatory testing with a published method and escalation rule, and no invented ceiling.
native_basis_label: the supplement as sold (as-packaged concentrate) — dry weight for powders, chews, tablets and capsules, neat liquid for oils and drops; no reconstitution, dilution, or as-fed conversion is applied
scope_note: Single-nutrient and multi-nutrient vitamin and mineral supplements for companion animals, in any as-sold dosage form (powder, tablet, capsule, soft chew, paste, liquid drop). This is the row where inorganic raw materials dominate: mineral salts and carbonates, trace-mineral concentrates, marine-derived mineral sources such as calcified seaweed, and clay, zeolite or diatomaceous-earth carriers and anti-caking agents are all recognised lead, cadmium and arsenic routes, and the ceilings below are held at full strictness for that reason rather than relaxed toward occurrence. Chromium may be a declared nutrient in this row, which is why total chromium is a control and hexavalent chromium is the species that binds. Boundary rules from the HMTc taxonomy govern placement: the product must be intended for animal consumption as a supplement rather than as the sole or primary diet; anything bearing an AAFCO nutritional adequacy statement routes to Category 17 (Pet Foods); and a dental chew routes to Category 17 (pet chews), because its primary function is food or treat rather than supplementation.
basis_guard: as sold|as_sold|as-sold|product as placed on (the )?market|as prepared for (wholesale|retail|consum)|finished product|by weight|dry weight|neat liquid|product as offered to consumer
basis_guard_note: Every named anchor must be a register row the register itself classifies basis_class=as_sold. A pet supplement is dosed as sold: a scoop of powder, a chew, a capsule, a pump of neat oil. It is never reconstituted, and the 8:1 powder-to-liquid conversion is confined to infant formula (CLAUDE.md Part 19), so no conversion is available to make a ready-to-feed liquid maximum comparable to an as-sold concentrate. The guard therefore blocks (a) every liquid/ready-to-feed limb of a form-split infant instrument, which the register classifies as_consumed, (b) the AU-NZ Schedule 19 'portion ordinarily consumed' rows, and (c) every animal-feed instrument, whose basis is a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification. Where a government instrument writes its own powder/liquid split and that instrument supplies the binding anchor, the guard mechanically selects the powder limb, which is what Method v2.0 step 4 requires: preserve the product-form split the government rule itself writes. That is the position on inorganic arsenic (EU 2023/915) and nickel (EU 2024/1987), the two cells where a form-split instrument still binds. It is not the position on lead, cadmium and total mercury: those three are anchored on Israel's FCS-2016 food-for-special-dietary-purpose limb, which is not form-split at all, so on those cells the guard does no limb selection and only confirms the row is written on the product as placed on market. Choosing the stricter liquid limb for an as-sold concentrate would be a silent basis conversion in the strict direction, which is still a conflation, and the as-consumed limbs declined on that ground are named cell by cell. 2026-09-02: the guard previously matched only the literal token as_sold (a native_basis label, not register basis text), so no in-force row could ever pass it; widened to the as-sold basis family.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default), pet-supplement double over-compliance form: the exact cell's only sovereign maximum is an animal-feed instrument, which is disclosed as a floor and never used; every published value is a disclosed read-across to the strictest applicable as-sold child-protective human-food sovereign maximum in the product's native as-sold basis, or a control where no as-sold sovereign value exists. Never occurrence-derived.

tAs.source_scope: Infant Milk substitute and Infant foods
tAs.label: Child-protective, human-grade read-across to the FSSAI total-arsenic maximum for infant milk substitute and infant foods, which the register records on an as-sold basis (the source column is parts per million by weight with no reconstitution basis stated). Total arsenic is a total-element cell in its own right and additionally gates the inorganic-arsenic speciation reflex; the toxic species is limited separately.
tAs.substantiation: No regulator in the default credible set sets a total-arsenic maximum for any child food: the EU, UK, Codex, US, Canadian and FSANZ instruments regulate inorganic arsenic only. The as-sold sovereign child-food total-arsenic rows are FSSAI (the strictest, adopted here), the Singapore Food Agency baby-food and infant-formula rows (sg_foodregs_2026_baby_food_tas_100, sg_foodregs_2026_infant_formula_tas_100), a Chinese milk-powder row and the Israeli formula-powder row (il_fcs2016_tas_14_1_infant_and_toddler_formulas_powder_1000). FSSAI is admitted to this category's credible-regulator set for that reason and it makes the standard stricter, not more convenient. The animal-feed floor that legally governs this cell is disclosed and never used: in the EU a pet supplement is complementary feed for pet animals or a feed additive under Directive 2002/32/EC and Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003 (register rows eu2002_32_pb_complementary_feed_10000, eu2002_32_cd_pet_complementary_feed_2000, eu2002_32_tas_complementary_feed_4000, eu2002_32_thg_mineral_feed_200, eu2002_32_pb_mineral_feed_15000, eu2002_32_cd_mineral_feed_materials_2000, eu2002_32_tas_mineral_feed_12000 and the trace-element and binder/anti-caking additive rows), with China's draft pet-feed guidance in the same range. Japan's Pet Food Safety Act is disclosed on the same footing and is the one pet-scoped floor that is neither draft nor guidance: the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food set statutory maxima that the register records on an as-sold basis for lead, cadmium and inorganic arsenic only (jp_petfood_2021_pb_3000, jp_petfood_2021_cd_1000, jp_petfood_2021_ias_2000), and set nothing for the remaining panel analytes. Category 17, the live pet-foods standard this category builds on, names the same three rows, and Category 18 names them here for the same reason. They run one hundred to three hundred times above the corresponding values published in this category. They are outside this compiler's audit scan because Japan sits outside this category's credible-regulator set, not because any basis mechanism blocks them; the honest statement is that HMTc declines them as a floor, not that the machinery could not see them. The human food-supplement floor (eu2023_cd_food_supplements_1000, th_moph414_2020_pb_food_supplement_1000, il_fcs2016_pb_17_dietary_supplements_3000, il_fcs2016_cd_16_dietary_supplements_except_listed_categories_1000, il_fcs2016_thg_15_dietary_supplements_100, gso193_2021_thg_food_supplements_100, asean2017_pb_health_supplements_10000, hsa2024_pb_health_supplements_10000) is likewise disclosed and never used. Of the three floors, only the EU feed rows are unreachable by construction: they carry a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification, so this row's basis guard blocks them and the audit scan drops any row whose basis names feed. The human food-supplement rows are not blocked by any mechanism at all — Israel's supplement rows are classified as-sold and match this row's audit scope — so they are declined by the declared analog-family filter alone, which is exactly why that filter is stated openly in _category.method_note instead of being left to the machinery to enforce silently. Register-tagging note for this cell, recorded because this cell's defensibility turns on the basis field. The FSSAI row's free-text basis previously read 'as consumed' while its basis_class read as_sold and its own notes recorded the as-sold correction against the FSSAI 2011 primary text, whose column header is parts per million by weight with no reconstitution basis stated — a half-applied correction that left the human-readable field contradicting the machine-readable one. The basis field now reads 'as sold', matching its already-corrected sibling in_sn_infant-milk-substitute-and-infant-foods_5000, and the same correction has been applied to the two other FSSAI Metal Contaminants infant rows that carried it (in_pb_infant-milk-substitute-and-infant-foods_200, in_cd_infant-milk-substitute-and-infant-foods_100). No value, scope or basis_class changed. The independent as-sold sweep returns one credible row stricter than this binding, il_fcs2016_tas_16_1_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_10, a packaged drinking-water ceiling in a different matrix; it is not adopted.

iAs.source_scope: infant formulae, follow-on formulae, food for special medical purposes intended for infants and young children, and young-child formulae placed on the market as powder
iAs.label: Child-protective, human-grade read-across to the powder limb of the EU 2023/915 inorganic-arsenic maximum for infant, follow-on, medical-purpose and young-child formula placed on the market as powder — the strictest as-sold sovereign inorganic-arsenic ceiling for a dry child-food concentrate.
iAs.substantiation: EU 2023/915 writes its own powder/liquid split for formula inorganic arsenic, and the EU as-sold baby-food row (eu2023_ias_babyfood_20) sits at the same value, so the powder limb and the general as-sold baby-food limb agree. The liquid limb (eu2023_ias_formula_liquid_10) governs a ready-to-feed liquid, is classified as_consumed, and is not applicable to an as-sold concentrate. The rice-specific child-food rows (fda2020_ias_infant_rice_cereal_100, us_ias_rice-cereals-for-infants-all-types-white_100, ca_ias_rice-based-foods-intended-specifically-f_100, uk_ias_rice-destined-for-the-production-of-food_100) are laxer and commodity-scoped. Rice-derived carriers (rice maltodextrin, rice flour, rice hull) are a recognised inorganic-arsenic route into supplement dosage forms and are held to this ceiling, not to the rice-commodity ceiling. Stricter-unselected audit disposition for this cell. The audit scan, whose scope is now identical on all seven subcategories, surfaces exactly one stricter row on every one of them: the Israeli fluid-milk inorganic-arsenic ceiling il_fcs2016_ias_1_milk_10. It is not adopted. The independent as-sold sweep additionally returns il_fcs2016_ias_16_1_bottled_drinking_water_and_mineral_water_6, a packaged drinking-water ceiling in a different matrix and consumption pattern that this compiler's water exclusion drops before the scan runs; it is named here rather than left out of scope, and it is not adopted. The general rule, stated once in _category.method_note and applied identically wherever it arises: the register's basis_class records whether a limit is written on the product as sold or as consumed, but it does not record how much water the commodity contains. A fresh vegetable and fluid milk are roughly seven-eighths to nine-tenths water, so their ceilings pass the as-sold basis guard while a face-value comparison against an as-sold dry concentrate understates them by close to an order of magnitude; on the dry-matter basis this row is sold in, each is looser than the anchor adopted here rather than stricter. They are also raw whole-commodity ceilings, and this category does not read a whole-commodity ceiling across to a concentrated dosage form. The reasoning is applicability reasoning only: no conversion is performed and no converted number is published anywhere in this category. The animal-feed floor that legally governs this cell is disclosed and never used: in the EU a pet supplement is complementary feed for pet animals or a feed additive under Directive 2002/32/EC and Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003 (register rows eu2002_32_pb_complementary_feed_10000, eu2002_32_cd_pet_complementary_feed_2000, eu2002_32_tas_complementary_feed_4000, eu2002_32_thg_mineral_feed_200, eu2002_32_pb_mineral_feed_15000, eu2002_32_cd_mineral_feed_materials_2000, eu2002_32_tas_mineral_feed_12000 and the trace-element and binder/anti-caking additive rows), with China's draft pet-feed guidance in the same range. Japan's Pet Food Safety Act is disclosed on the same footing and is the one pet-scoped floor that is neither draft nor guidance: the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food set statutory maxima that the register records on an as-sold basis for lead, cadmium and inorganic arsenic only (jp_petfood_2021_pb_3000, jp_petfood_2021_cd_1000, jp_petfood_2021_ias_2000), and set nothing for the remaining panel analytes. Category 17, the live pet-foods standard this category builds on, names the same three rows, and Category 18 names them here for the same reason. They run one hundred to three hundred times above the corresponding values published in this category. They are outside this compiler's audit scan because Japan sits outside this category's credible-regulator set, not because any basis mechanism blocks them; the honest statement is that HMTc declines them as a floor, not that the machinery could not see them. The human food-supplement floor (eu2023_cd_food_supplements_1000, th_moph414_2020_pb_food_supplement_1000, il_fcs2016_pb_17_dietary_supplements_3000, il_fcs2016_cd_16_dietary_supplements_except_listed_categories_1000, il_fcs2016_thg_15_dietary_supplements_100, gso193_2021_thg_food_supplements_100, asean2017_pb_health_supplements_10000, hsa2024_pb_health_supplements_10000) is likewise disclosed and never used. Of the three floors, only the EU feed rows are unreachable by construction: they carry a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification, so this row's basis guard blocks them and the audit scan drops any row whose basis names feed. The human food-supplement rows are not blocked by any mechanism at all — Israel's supplement rows are classified as-sold and match this row's audit scope — so they are declined by the declared analog-family filter alone, which is exactly why that filter is stated openly in _category.method_note instead of being left to the machinery to enforce silently. Divergence from HMTc Category 16, disclosed. Category 16 anchors inorganic arsenic on eu2023_ias_formula_liquid_10 and publishes 10 ug/kg for as-sold solid supplements; Category 18 declines that row because the register classifies it as_consumed, and reads the powder limb of the same instrument at 20 ug/kg instead. This category publishes the laxer of the two numbers and says so. The reason is the basis rule rather than a policy preference, and no stricter as-sold sovereign inorganic-arsenic instrument exists anywhere in the credible set for a non-water, non-fluid-commodity matrix, so there is nothing available to close the gap without performing the conversion Method v2.0 forbids. The reconciliation belongs on the Category 16 side and is logged with the aluminium item.

The human food-supplement floor (eu2023_cd_food_supplements_1000, th_moph414_2020_pb_food_supplement_1000, il_fcs2016_pb_17_dietary_supplements_3000, il_fcs2016_cd_16_dietary_supplements_except_listed_categories_1000, il_fcs2016_thg_15_dietary_supplements_100, gso193_2021_thg_food_supplements_100, asean2017_pb_health_supplements_10000, hsa2024_pb_health_supplements_10000) is likewise disclosed and never used. This category publishes the laxer of the two numbers and says so. The reconciliation belongs on the Category 16 side and is logged with the aluminium item.

Sn.binding_control: Container class is a certification precondition on this cell, not a variable ceiling. The published tin value governs every lot certified under Category 18 without exception. Tin-coated or otherwise unlacquered metal-can primary packaging is out of scope for this row; no alternate canned limb is offered, and eu2023_sn_canned_infant_formula_50000 and eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000 are expressly excluded as substitute ceilings. Any quantifiable tin on a non-canned lot is treated as a packaging or contact-material finding and triggers a container investigation before release.
Sn.basis: the supplement as sold (as-packaged concentrate) — dry weight for powders, chews, tablets and capsules, neat liquid for oils and drops; no reconstitution, dilution, or as-fed conversion is applied
Sn.source_scope: Infant Milk substitute and Infant foods
Sn.label: Child-protective, human-grade read-across to the FSSAI tin maximum for infant milk substitute and infant foods — the only as-sold, non-canned sovereign child-food tin ceiling on the register.
Sn.substantiation: Tin in food is overwhelmingly a can-migration analyte: every other child-food tin maximum on the register is scoped to canned product (eu2023_sn_canned_infant_formula_50000, eu2023_sn_canned_babyfood_cereal_50000, uk_sn_canned-baby-foods-and-canned-processed-c_50000 and their equivalents) and the general canned-food ceiling is eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000. A pet supplement in a tub, bottle, sachet, blister or soft-chew pouch has no tin-coated contact surface and therefore no migration pathway, so the non-canned FSSAI row is the applicable analog rather than any canned ceiling. Any quantifiable tin on a non-canned lot is treated as a packaging or contact-material finding and triggers a container investigation before release. Container-class determination, stated so that the ceiling an auditor applies is fixed by this document rather than selectable after the fact. There is no alternate tin limb in Category 18. A lot presented in tin-coated or otherwise unlacquered metal-can primary packaging is not certifiable under this row: neither eu2023_sn_canned_infant_formula_50000 (50,000 ug/kg, the child-protective canned limb) nor eu2023_sn_canned_foods_200000 (200,000 ug/kg, the general-population canned limb) is available here as a substitute ceiling, and the published value applies to every certified lot without exception. Such a product is out of scope for Category 18 certification pending a separate container-class determination, which would be a new published row with its own anchor and its own audit trail rather than a discretionary alternate path inside this one. The animal-feed floor that legally governs this cell is disclosed and never used: in the EU a pet supplement is complementary feed for pet animals or a feed additive under Directive 2002/32/EC and Regulation (EC) No 1831/2003 (register rows eu2002_32_pb_complementary_feed_10000, eu2002_32_cd_pet_complementary_feed_2000, eu2002_32_tas_complementary_feed_4000, eu2002_32_thg_mineral_feed_200, eu2002_32_pb_mineral_feed_15000, eu2002_32_cd_mineral_feed_materials_2000, eu2002_32_tas_mineral_feed_12000 and the trace-element and binder/anti-caking additive rows), with China's draft pet-feed guidance in the same range. Japan's Pet Food Safety Act is disclosed on the same footing and is the one pet-scoped floor that is neither draft nor guidance: the FAMIC Specifications and Standards of Pet Food set statutory maxima that the register records on an as-sold basis for lead, cadmium and inorganic arsenic only (jp_petfood_2021_pb_3000, jp_petfood_2021_cd_1000, jp_petfood_2021_ias_2000), and set nothing for the remaining panel analytes. Category 17, the live pet-foods standard this category builds on, names the same three rows, and Category 18 names them here for the same reason. They run one hundred to three hundred times above the corresponding values published in this category. They are outside this compiler's audit scan because Japan sits outside this category's credible-regulator set, not because any basis mechanism blocks them; the honest statement is that HMTc declines them as a floor, not that the machinery could not see them. The human food-supplement floor (eu2023_cd_food_supplements_1000, th_moph414_2020_pb_food_supplement_1000, il_fcs2016_pb_17_dietary_supplements_3000, il_fcs2016_cd_16_dietary_supplements_except_listed_categories_1000, il_fcs2016_thg_15_dietary_supplements_100, gso193_2021_thg_food_supplements_100, asean2017_pb_health_supplements_10000, hsa2024_pb_health_supplements_10000) is likewise disclosed and never used. Of the three floors, only the EU feed rows are unreachable by construction: they carry a 12%-moisture feed basis with no as_sold classification, so this row's basis guard blocks them and the audit scan drops any row whose basis names feed. The human food-supplement rows are not blocked by any mechanism at all — Israel's supplement rows are classified as-sold and match this row's audit scope — so they are declined by the declared analog-family filter alone, which is exactly why that filter is stated openly in _category.method_note instead of being left to the machinery to enforce silently.

Al.rationale: No government anywhere sets an aluminium contaminant maximum for a food on an as-sold basis. The only sovereign food aluminium numbers on the register are the FSANZ Schedule 19 infant-formula rows — aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500 at 500 ug/kg for non-soy infant, follow-on and special-medical-purpose formula, and aunz_sch19_al_formula_soy_1000 at 1000 ug/kg for soy-based formula — which are written on a 'portion ordinarily consumed' reconstituted basis the register classifies as_consumed and which no permitted conversion makes comparable to an as-sold concentrate, and the Chinese GB 2760 baked-goods and starch-noodle rows, which are permitted food-additive residue allowances for alum firming and leavening agents rather than contaminant ceilings. The remaining aluminium rows are drinking-water guideline values and a plastics food-contact specific migration limit, both different matrices in different bases. Adopting the reconstituted FSANZ value for an as-sold powder would be a silent eight-fold basis conversion in the strict direction; adopting an additive-residue allowance as a contaminant ceiling would misdescribe the instrument. Neither is supportable, so no number is invented and testing is mandatory instead. This is the same disposition HMTc Category 17 publishes for aluminium in pet foods. Divergence from HMTc Category 16, disclosed here because this is the one cell where Category 18 publishes no ceiling and the live human-supplement standard publishes one. Category 16 reads aunz_sch19_al_formula_nonsoy_500 across to as-sold solid supplements and publishes 500 ug/kg, describing it there as the only government aluminium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction. Category 18 declines the same row on basis grounds, and the consequence is stated plainly rather than left to be discovered: a pet supplement certified under Category 18 receives no numeric aluminium ceiling, only mandatory measurement and a trend control, where a human supplement certified under Category 16 receives 500 ug/kg. Category 18's basis reasoning is the more rigorous of the two, and the reconciliation belongs on the Category 16 side, which is the side performing an undisclosed as-consumed to as-sold read; it is logged for that purpose and is not resolved from inside this config.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium on every lot by ICP-MS after closed-vessel microwave acid digestion. Results are trended per SKU and per raw-material lot; a step change against the SKU's own established baseline, or any result attributable to a declared aluminium-bearing processing aid, anti-caking agent, colour lake or clay/zeolite carrier, triggers a formulation and raw-material investigation before release. Aluminium results are reported on the certificate rather than suppressed.
